critique.reason: The proposed $3,000 credit does not match the contract. MSA-NW-2025 §4.2 sets the credit at 0.5% of the monthly platform fee ($500) for each full hour of unavailability beyond the 99.9% commitment in §4.1, and caps the credit at $1,000 per calendar month. TCK-881 records 6h15m of unavailability on 2026-09-14, so the calculation is 6 hours at $500 = $3,000 before the cap, and the $1,000 cap then limits the credit. Excluding the monthly allowance under §4.1 would give 5 full hours, or $2,500, before the cap, so the cap controls under either reading and the supported credit is $1,000. CRM-2207 was sent 2026-09-26, within the 30-day written-request window in §4.2, so the claim is timely, but the amount is capped. Under §4.2 the credit is the customer's sole remedy for unavailability, and §7.4 bars withholding or set-off except a §4.2 credit. Northwind paid $97,000 against a $100,000 invoice (INV-1001). Only the $1,000 credit may be deducted; the remaining $2,000 is an unauthorized set-off and stays due. The invoice was due 2026-10-01 under the Net 30 terms in §3.2, so the $2,000 balance is now past due and may accrue 1% per month under §3.2. The credit memo should be issued for $1,000 and the $2,000 shortfall collected.
